causal_mechanism.definition: Recurring institutional, commercial, or systematic schedules cause risk to be reallocated around known calendar windows.
Information reflected first in one market is subsequently incorporated into a related market.
Participants adjust accumulated inventory over time because immediate transfer is costly or incomplete.
State-dependent hedging demand changes with market movement and feeds back into further movement.
A temporary price-insensitive flow ends, allowing prices to adjust after its pressure dissipates.
Deteriorating funding or balance-sheet capacity compels participants to reduce risk exposures.
Liquidity providers reduce risk-bearing capacity when uncertainty or adverse-selection risk rises.

counterparty.definition: Participants whose risk taking is limited by funding, leverage, capital, or balance-sheet capacity.
Intermediaries that warehouse or dynamically hedge customer and market risk.
Participants or markets that incorporate public information relatively early.
Participants compelled to reduce exposures by risk, leverage, mandate, or funding constraints.
Participants transferring pre-existing economic or inventory risk rather than seeking standalone exposure.
Participants or markets that incorporate public information relatively late.
Participants requiring prompt execution and consuming available liquidity.
Participants supplying immediacy and bearing inventory or adverse-selection risk.
Participants willing and able to hold transferred risk without immediate rebalancing pressure.
Participants reallocating risk under recurring mandates, benchmarks, or systematic schedules.
Participants with comparatively flexible funding and capacity to absorb transferred risk.

expected_effect.definition: A related market adjusts as already-public information diffuses across markets.
Risk bearers receive compensation over the stated economic horizon without implying a trading rule.
Prices reflect compensation for scarce immediacy or impaired risk-bearing capacity.
An economic feedback mechanism increases continuation of contemporaneous market movement.
A source-supported market move tends to persist over the classified economic horizon.
A source-supported price displacement tends to unwind after its economic cause dissipates.
Price variability or dispersion rises during the classified economic context.

holding_horizon.definition: The economic effect is expected to develop and substantially resolve within a trading session, without specifying an exact timeframe.
The economic effect belongs to the duration of a bounded liquidity or flow episode, without specifying bar size or clock parameters.
The economic effect is expected to span more than one trading session without an exact holding-period parameter.
The economic effect belongs to a recurring named calendar window without an exact strategy holding period.
The economic effect connects one completed session or market period to the next.
The economic effect evolves over a broad macro, positioning, or balance-sheet interval rather than an execution timeframe.

information_availability.definition: The information is first usable only after a specified public event has occurred.
The information is first usable only after the source-defined observation interval is complete.
The information is available from a completed prior reporting or market period.
The public information becomes observable while the relevant market event is unfolding.
The information becomes public only after a documented reporting or publication delay.
The classification is publicly known before the relevant event or window begins.
The event schedule is known beforehand while additional public information arrives during the event.
information_availability.display_label: Known schedule with live public information

information_input.definition: A recurring calendar classification known independently of subsequent market outcomes.
Public or governed measures of funding conditions, leverage, capital, or balance-sheet capacity.
A source-bound proxy for participant positioning, inventory, or risk-transfer demand.
Observed market prices available at the relevant decision time, without specifying a derived indicator or rule.
Public content released by an identified issuer, agency, exchange, or institution.
Observed public quote, spread, and order-book depth information without a prescribed calculation.
Observed public price or transaction information from an economically related market.
The pre-announced timing and identity of a public market-relevant event.
Observed public transaction activity or signed-flow information without a prescribed trigger or parameter.
Observed public volatility or option-risk state information without an indicator rule or parameterization.

instrument.definition: CME E-mini S&P 500 equity index futures represented as a continuous research instrument, excluding any particular contract month.
CME E-mini Nasdaq-100 equity index futures represented as a continuous research instrument, excluding any particular contract month.

market_behavior.definition: A reduction in intermediaries' or investors' capacity to hold or finance market risk.
Risk-management transactions that reinforce contemporaneous market movement through endogenous feedback.
Publicly observable information is incorporated across related markets at different speeds.
Outstanding dealer, intermediary, or participant inventory creates pressure to transfer or rebalance risk.
Available liquidity becomes temporarily scarce or unusually costly relative to prevailing conditions.
Transactions are driven primarily by constraints or mandates rather than contemporaneous valuation choice.
Recurring calendar-linked risk reallocations create predictable pressure on market positioning.

market_context.definition: Regular continuous trading outside a separately classified auction or scheduled-event context.
The phenomenon depends on economic linkage between distinct markets or asset classes.
Participants face forced exposure reduction or widespread risk liquidation.
Funding costs or balance-sheet constraints materially impair risk-bearing capacity.
Market depth or immediacy is unusually scarce relative to ordinary conditions.
The market-opening price-discovery and risk-transfer process.
A publicly known option-expiration window in which option risk transfer may affect underlying futures.
A publicly scheduled announcement window associated with changing information and liquidity conditions.
A recurring and publicly classifiable calendar period associated with risk reallocation.
A boundary between completed and newly active trading sessions or market periods.

transfer_rationale.definition: Returns compensate capital that supplies balance-sheet capacity when others are constrained.
Returns compensate capital that accommodates recurring calendar-linked risk transfers.
Returns arise because risk-management demand affects prices faced by other participants.
Returns accrue to participants or markets that process public information before slower counterparts.
Returns compensate capital for absorbing or carrying inventory risk transferred by others.
Returns compensate participants for supplying immediacy under adverse-selection or inventory risk.
Returns compensate patient capital for trading against participants with constrained execution timing.

cross_field_invariants.definition: Cross-asset behavior, mechanism, effect, or context requires related-market public information.
Funding and balance-sheet classifications require a funding or balance-sheet information category.
Endogenous hedging feedback requires an option-risk or positioning/inventory input category.
Option-expiration context requires the scheduled-event calendar and volatility/option-risk information categories.
Scheduled-announcement context requires a scheduled-event calendar and information known before or mixed with live public release.
Seasonal behavior, mechanism, horizon, or context requires a calendar-seasonality information category.

description: Small, general economic concepts for pre-hypothesis futures discovery memory. The taxonomy classifies economic identity only and grants no P1 evidence, approval, admission, strategy, or deployment authority.
